<p class="section-kicker">RESEARCH PROGRAM</p>

## Three connected lines of inquiry

::: {.research-grid}
::: {.research-card}
<span class="card-index">01</span>

### Visual intelligence

How can multimodal systems retain the right evidence, reason across images and language, and reveal where their conclusions become unreliable?

`Computer Vision` `VLMs` `Evaluation`
:::

::: {.research-card}
<span class="card-index">02</span>

### Trustworthy AI

How do we make model behavior easier to test, challenge, reproduce, and audit—especially under adversarial or ambiguous conditions?

`AI Security` `Robustness` `Integrity`
:::

::: {.research-card}
<span class="card-index">03</span>

### Quantitative ML

How can learning systems support decisions when signals are noisy, risks are asymmetric, and confidence matters as much as a prediction?

`Forecasting` `Risk` `Decision Systems`
:::
:::

### NoveltyAudit

An evidence-first agent skill for adversarial scholarly novelty audits. It decomposes claims, constructs minimal prior sets, respects historical cutoffs, and exposes bridge-dependent prior-work arguments.

[View repository ↗](https://github.com/niansia/NoveltyAudit){.project-link}

<p class="section-kicker light">HOW I WORK</p>

## Research should survive contact with reality.
:::

::: {.principles-list}
<div><span>01</span><p><strong>Start with the failure case.</strong><br>Define what would make the idea unconvincing before optimizing the benchmark.</p></div>
<div><span>02</span><p><strong>Keep evidence inspectable.</strong><br>Build pipelines whose data, assumptions, and intermediate decisions can be traced.</p></div>
<div><span>03</span><p><strong>Turn theory into artifacts.</strong><br>Use prototypes to expose questions that remain invisible in abstract discussion.</p></div>
:::
:::
